mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates and supports equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns through earnings deterioration.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicate a contraction in real economic activity, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls > 1% and INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: HOUST falls > 1% and INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 3 months but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), higher discount rates and reduced liquidity cause negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained employment level above 130,000 thousand persons indicates strong consumer spending, producing positive 5-day S&P 500 returns through elevated corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS is above 130,000.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level below 500 thousand units signals weak consumer demand in the construction sector, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: HOUST falls < 500 but SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (above 0.5%) combined with high unemployment (UNRATE > 8.5%) indicates monetary tightening in a weak labor market, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE > 8.5% but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO < 95) reduces corporate output and earnings, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 returns during supply-constrained economic regimes.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95 but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances.
